items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, TLS coverage, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. TLS reports no certificates expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS posture. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 35 pass, 14 fail, 10 unknown. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of compromise. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive release, medium for bounded reversible growth. Exact decision: continue existing read-only security evidence work and failure containment; permit only reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, provenance, and claims boundaries. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, change permissions, deploy, add dependencies, expand public exposure, or conduct external outreach.

Security handoff: continue the existing bounded read-only evidence matrix only. Record dated evidence, owners, affected scope, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data flows, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not create duplicate telemetry requests or new production work.
